title: Pseudo-coherence under a quotient between flat finitely presented algebras
statement: Let $R\to B\xrightarrow{q} A$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings, with $q$ surjective and both $R\to B$ and $R\to A$ flat and of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map, def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. In ordinary module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], for every $M\in D(A)$, the object $M$ is pseudo-coherent over $A$ if and only if its restriction of scalars along $q$ is pseudo-coherent over $B$ [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex]. Here restriction of scalars applies the ordinary forgetful functor termwise to a complex. There is no Noetherian hypothesis.

proof.text: Choose a finite polynomial presentation $\pi:P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow B$ using [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra] and the polynomial ring of [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. The composite $q\pi:P\to A$ is surjective: lift an element first through $q$ and then through $\pi$. Thus the same $P$ presents both algebras. On any complex representing $M$, direct restriction along $q\pi$ and successive restriction along $q$ and $\pi$ give the same $P$-action, namely $p\cdot m=q(\pi(p))m$, with identical groups and differentials. Forgetting scalars keeps kernels, images and cohomology, so this identification is valid in the derived categories.

source.place: Tag 0E1T, lemma-more-relative-pseudo-coherent-is-moot, polynomial-presentation reformulation of its relative comparisons; definition-relatively-pseudo-coherent.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-flat-fp-polynomial-pseudocoherent] to $R\to B$ with presentation $\pi$ and to $R\to A$ with presentation $q\pi$. Both maps are flat and finitely presented by the hypotheses of the item; both chosen presentations are surjective by step 1. Hence $B[0]$ and $A[0]$ are pseudo-coherent over this same ring $P$. No Noetherian assumption on $P$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 067J, lemma-flat-finite-presentation-perfect, pseudo-coherence consequence; Tag 065H, lemma-relatively-pseudo-coherent, arbitrary presentation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-pseudocoherent-algebra-scalar-restriction] to $P\to A$ and $M$, using the pseudo-coherence of $A[0]$ from step 2. This gives $M$ pseudo-coherent over $A$ if and only if $(q\pi)_*M$ is pseudo-coherent over $P$. Apply the same lemma to $P\to B$ and $q_*M$, using pseudo-coherence of $B[0]$: $q_*M$ is pseudo-coherent over $B$ if and only if $\pi_*(q_*M)$ is pseudo-coherent over $P$. The two right-hand complexes agree by the explicit action calculation in step 1. Combining the equivalences proves both implications for every $M\in D(A)$.
